subject: questions about type and rho in lavaan.survey

messages.author: 90bf4023f1fff3d8
messages.subject: questions about type and rho in lavaan.survey
parts:
Hi, Lavaan users:

  I have two quick questions about lavaan.survey.

  Q1. How many options do we have for type? I only know "Fay". In the dataset I am using, they only specified there were Balanced Repeated Replication (BRR). No specification about what method was applied for BRR.

  Q2. How may we obtain rho for BRR? BRR were provided. Is it just the average correlation for BRR?

  Would appreciate if any of you may help.

  Thanks.

Grace

messages.author: 90bf4023f1fff3d8
messages.subject: Re: questions about type and rho in lavaan.survey
parts:
Some additional information: it was specified that they used "Hadamard" matrix, an orthogonal matrix for calculating BRR.

Would appreciate any help.

Grace

messages.author: b8fd92e5e3662745
messages.subject: Re: questions about type and rho in lavaan.survey
parts:
If nothing is said about the BRR weights, then you don't need the Fay correction, and you don't need the rho. (It is unfortunate that Thomas Lumley referred to this factor as rho in library(survey), for the confusion it apparently creates. It is NOT a correlation of any kind.)

To check whether these assumptions are warranted, you can summary() the main weights and a handful of BRR weights. If the minimum is zero, and the maximum is about twice the maximum of the main weights, then these weights do not have any Fay corrections attached.

messages.subject: Re: questions about type and rho in lavaan.survey
parts:
Thanks, Stas.

I checked a moment ago. Yes, the minimum is 0 and the maximum is about twice the maximum of  sampling weights or analytic weight. Therefore, type=BRR would work out, right?

I also double checked the data file. In the documentation, it is specified:
 "First, the conditional probability of selection for the students was applied to the corresponding school-level replicate weight to form the student BRR base weights. Second, the two nonresponse adjustments discussed previously were applied to each set of base weights. Finally, student-level BRR weights were calibrated to the sampling frame. The nonresponse-adjusted replicate weights were calibrated to the control totals to form the 200 final student BRR weights.'

 So, the combined.weights=TRUE.

Appreciate your help. Now, I can move forward.

Thanks again.

Grace
